clue.text: Note the girl in charge is exemplary

parts.note: C is a musical note
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Praise for a young woman who runs things impeccably.
explanation.definitionFit: Something classic serves as a model of its kind, the standard others copy.

clue.text: Cover can include a top man

indicators.note: include says the tin takes the letter inside itself

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A lid for a tin can contain a leader.

clue.text: Leading in any lawlessness

parts.note: arch means chief or leading, as in archbishop

explanation.definitionFit: A slide is a fall or deterioration, as in a slide in prices.

clue.text: Well aware caning's to effect reform

parts.note: the word written with its s

clue.text: This might be just the thing!

definitions.text: This might be just the thing!

parts.words: This might be just the thing!
parts.note: the word 'the' is a grammatical item of exactly this kind, and a thing is also called one in everyday speech

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation sounds like delight at finding something suitable, but read literally 'the' is the definite one in grammar, and 'thing' is another meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' is the definite one of these words, and an item or object is also called this.

clue.text: Like a small house in Berkshire

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons

explanation.surface: Describing a cottage in a southern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a Berkshire town known for its racecourse; the definition reads as 'a place in Berkshire'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a town in the English county of Berkshire, home of a famous racecourse.

clue.text: Bully people in high places

men are people

clue.text: Figure an adieu should be taken in song

clue.text: Oriental lands willingly left

states are lands or countries

explanation.definitionFit: Property bequeathed in a will is the deceased's estate.

clue.text: The joiner's 25 work

explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion caused' rearranges CLAIMS and THE together.

clue.text: Out of work, that's true

clue.text: An irresolute poet?

clue.text: Feeling making an onset is quite wrong

indicators.note: wrong letters are out of order, so the words before are rearranged

clue.text: Alas it's an excitable breed of dog

clue.text: Money grabbed by person not known to be criminal

indicators.note: grabbed by says the money is held inside the person

parts.note: a stranger is someone you do not know
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.definitionFit: A strangler is a killer who throttles victims, so a lawbreaker.

clue.text: A cross on a church carpet

a minster is a large church

explanation.definitionFit: A woven pile rug type named after a town in Devon where it was first made.

clue.text: Having no end in view

parts.note: end is read as goal or purpose, and a person with none is drifting

explanation.definitionFit: Without purpose or goal, drifting.

clue.text: A French writer's story set in the ruins of Rome

indicators.note: set in means the story is put inside the other letters
the ruins of a word are its letters scattered and reordered

parts.note: a lie is a story, a falsehood

explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins of' rearranges ROME as MORE; 'set in' puts LIE inside it after MO.

clue.text: Go over and gather around the Conservative leader

indicators.note: the leader of the word Conservative is its first letter

explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise or review points again, a short form of recapitulate.

clue.text: Firm arrangement

clue.text: He'll display mean notice with little hesitation

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who parades marches or shows off publicly.

clue.text: Some dismal tavern in a foreign country

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'in a foreign country' as the definition; 'in' is a link word, since the answer is the country itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is an island state in the Mediterranean, abroad from a British point of view.

clue.text: He acknowledges to study harder is essential

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

clue.text: A time for 9
